PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 77 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 11/14/25 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of persistent lower extremity edema, and ongoing fatigue assessment.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit with notable concerns regarding his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), persistent bilateral lower extremity edema, and ongoing fatigue. Since his last visit, he reports a slight improvement in his respiratory symptoms; however, nocturnal wheezing episodes continue to occur, particularly when lying flat. He has been compliant with the adjusted medication regimen, including the addition of a long-acting muscarinic antagonist (LAMA), tiotropium, which he states has provided some relief during the day, but he still experiences shortness of breath during exertion.
The bilateral lower extremity edema remains a significant issue. Mr. Fairfax notes that despite increasing the furosemide dosage to 80 mg daily, the swelling persists at 1+ pitting, particularly exacerbated by prolonged periods of sitting. He denies any associated pain, redness, or warmth but expresses concern regarding the impact on his mobility and quality of life.
His fatigue continues unabated, described as a debilitating level of tiredness that is not relieved by rest. He reports a decreased ability to engage in social activities and has been feeling increasingly isolated. He mentions that sleep disturbances persist, primarily due to discomfort from the edema and anxiety related to his health.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, + dyspnea on exertion, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, increased use to three times daily due to increased symptoms. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily (new addition). 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 80 mg daily (increased dosage).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.7F, HR 80, BP 128/78, RR 20, O2 sat 90% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress but appears fatigued and slightly anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.3, Hgb 12.6, Hct 37.2, Plt 220 2. BMP: Na 135, K 4.1, Cl 95, CO2 25, BUN 18, Cr 1.2, Glucose 86 3. BNP: 460 (slightly elevated). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.4 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: The addition of tiotropium appears to provide some benefit, but nocturnal symptoms persist. Continue current regimen and consider a nighttime dose of albuterol as needed. Follow-up in 1 month to reassess symptoms and medication efficacy. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema continues despite increased furosemide. Reinforce dietary sodium restrictions and encourage Mr. Fairfax to elevate his legs regularly. Consider referral to nephrology for further evaluation if no improvement is noted in the next follow-up. 4. Fatigue: Given the ongoing fatigue and lack of significant findings on laboratory tests, consider referral to a psychologist for evaluation of potential depression and anxiety management strategies. Schedule follow-up CBC and metabolic panel in one month to monitor for any changes.
Patient education reiterated regarding recognizing signs of exacerbation, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
